title: Recognising and Comparing Proper Fractions
introduction: Explore recognising and comparing proper fractions using everyday examples.
definition: A proper positive fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator. Use equally sized parts of the same whole. For Year 2 practise denominators up to ten and compare simple fractions using drawings.

examples.question: Compare 1/4 and 3/4.
steps: Both have four equal parts; three selected parts exceed one.

exercises.question: Numerator of 3/8?
exercises.solution: The numerator is the top number, which counts selected parts. In 3/8 it is 3.

exercises.question: Denominator of 7/10?
exercises.solution: The denominator is the bottom number, which counts all equal parts. In 7/10 it is 10.

exercises.question: Which numerator is bigger in 2/5 and 4/5?
exercises.solution: Both fractions have denominator 5; compare numerators: 4 > 2.

exercises.question: How many fourths make a whole?
Write three of ten equal parts as a fraction.
exercises.solution: There are 3 selected parts out of 10 equal parts, giving 3/10.

summary: A proper positive fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator. Use equally sized parts of the same whole. For Year 2 practise denominators up to ten and compare simple fractions using drawings.
